title: RingedRefinementCoherences
statement: For any normalized ringed Calculus o, Spatial p, ScalarComparisons sc, ScalarComposition ac and OpenComparisons e on a scheme T in either mode, the canonical adjunct refinements satisfy ElementaryCoherences sc ac (canonicalRefinements e), and ElementaryShifts sc e is nonempty (inverse-scalar comparison, clopen projection and geometric adjunction compatibility for the universally fixed scalar shifts). In particular the scalar/geometric h-square is an equality before proper-adjunction transposition, and coefficient and refinement composition, unit and spatial equations hold.

source.place: 6.7.6–6.7.7, compactification independence; agent ordinary-derived ring-sheaf coefficient supplement to the clopen-section refinement construction, not a theorem literally asserted in the paper.

proof.text:
restrict the inverse beta and delta comparisons to their defining open
units. Their compatibility is then the coherent scalar/pullback compositor.
The clopen decomposition is an exact product equivalence on complexes and derived
categories; scalar extension preserves its identity/zero projection. Paste this
projection equation with beta and open composition to obtain `h_compatible`.
The section/retraction compositor agrees on both coefficient sides by pullback
composition coherence. The coefficient cocycle and units are obtained from the
normalized projection cocycle, using the balanced associators fixed on pure
tensors and on K-flat representatives; transposition similarly gives the open
coefficient and unit equations. For successive refinements, the nested clopen
projections both have matrix (identity, zero, zero). Paste their normalized open
comparisons, then take mates to obtain refinement composition; selecting the whole
component gives the identity. Spatial coefficient compatibility follows by pasting
the two inverse-image/scalar squares and taking mates. Exact open operations act
termwise; scalar shifts are fixed by the universal cochain counits. The derived
adjunction shift equations give compatibility of the geometric unit and counit.
Formal assembly derives shifts of beta and delta from their specified inverse transposes, then derives shifts of h from its three factors. It also derives shifts of chi, the refinement and both square composites. Assembly constructs scalar shifts and their counit compatibility from the universal property. Assembly also proves compatibility of the geometric adjunction from the standard K-injective shift construction and its derived unit formula. Only inverse-scalar and pi compatibility remain in this obligation. The same proofs work on the actual
vertical sites, retaining all semilinear transitions.

proof_origin.place: The indicated construction steps of the ordinary-derived coefficient supplement to 6.7.6--6.7.7.
